title: Power Automate: direct triggers for desktop flows
summary: Hold: Microsoft Learn now documents Scheduled triggers in preview, including configuration, disabling schedules, prerequisites and environment-wide Operator permissions. The briefing's blanket statements that direct triggering has no documentation or controls are no longer accurate; the roadmap dates remain correct, and the documented scheduling capability should not be presented as proof that every planned event trigger has shipped.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe direct triggers for desktop flows.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide availability switch or corresponding tenant-wide API for direct triggers is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers disable tenant environment setting PowerShell Power Platform API Dataverse trigger table. Opened desktop-flows/governance, schedule-desktop-flows and flowtrigger table reference; these document machine or per-schedule controls, not a tenant-wide switch.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: There is no documented setting for direct triggers, so nothing can be configured or disabled yet.
claims.quote: Select Disable for an enabled trigger. Select Enable for a disabled trigger. Disabling a scheduled trigger stops future scheduled runs without deleting its configuration.
claims.fix: Replace 'nothing to configure yet', 'nothing to disable before the preview' and the blanket no-setting statements with: 'No tenant-wide availability switch is documented. For Scheduled triggers (preview), the Power Automate route is Automation center > Manage > Scheduled triggers (Preview) > Overview > scheduled trigger > More commands > Disable; disabling stops future scheduled runs.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows. Keep the tenant-wide row's null sides, but narrow its note to that tenant-wide gap rather than claiming no per-schedule controls exist.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy reaches the data-policy control.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. In the Data protection and privacy screen, select the Data policy section. Select + New Policy.
claims.fix: The printed route reaches the policy list, not connector classification. Extend it to 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > Assign connectors' as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/prevent-data-loss.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates a data policy using a policy-definition object.
claims.quote: Creates a new DLP policy in the tenant by using the NewPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition object. New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy
claims.fix: Retain the call, and clarify in the row note that it creates a policy from a supplied definition rather than editing existing connector classifications. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/data-loss-prevention-sdk, which documents policy creation with Business, Non-business and Blocked classifications, alongside the cmdlet reference.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern desktop flow modules in environments.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.claim: The desktop flow connector can be governed like other connectors.
claims.quote: The desktop flow connector can be governed in your policies like any other connector in all environments.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how direct triggers themselves are governed.
claims.quote: users assigned the Power Automate Operator role can manage desktop-flow schedules, in addition to the schedule owner. They can create, view, update, enable or disable, and delete schedules.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket governance absence with: 'For Scheduled triggers (preview), the schedule owner and users assigned the Power Automate Operator role can manage schedules. Operator permissions for Flow trigger and Flow trigger instance apply across the environment and do not grant permission to edit the desktop flow definition.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows. Retain only the narrower unresolved question about connector-policy enforcement on the new triggering route.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether desktop flow connector policies govern the new direct triggering route.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers data policies connector governance; Scheduled triggers desktop flows licensing data policies. Opened prevent-data-loss and schedule-desktop-flows; the former governs modules and the connector, while the latter does not specify connector-policy enforcement.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the default or how users opt into direct triggering.
claims.quote: On Scheduled triggers, select New. To activate the trigger immediately after you create it, turn on Enable. Leave it off to save the trigger as disabled.
claims.fix: Use 'user-opt-in' for the documented Scheduled triggers preview and state: 'Users create a scheduled trigger and choose Enable to activate it; leaving Enable off saves it disabled. Microsoft has not stated arrival behaviour for any broader event-trigger capability beyond this documented scheduling preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows and narrow the default-related open question accordingly.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no licensing requirement for direct triggering is published.
claims.quote: The licensing and capacity required for the selected attended or unattended run mode.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'mixed' and replace the blanket unknown requirement with: 'Scheduled triggers (preview) require the licensing and capacity for the selected attended or unattended run mode. Power Automate Premium includes attended desktop automation; the licensing overview directs unattended desktop flows to Process licenses or pay-as-you-go. No direct-trigger-specific licensing change is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows and the already cited licensing overview.

claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop flows direct triggers licensing prerequisites; Scheduled triggers desktop flows licensing. Opened schedule-desktop-flows and power-automate-licensing/types; the scheduling page requires existing run-mode licensing and names no trigger-specific change.

claims.claim: The cloud-triggering page requires the appropriate licence for attended runs.
claims.quote: To run the triggered desktop flows, you need to have the appropriate license (for attended runs)

claims.quote: For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.quote: Power Automate flow runs (preview) | Flow runs for premium cloud flows and desktop flows.

claims.claim: Attended desktop-run charges in pay-as-you-go environments depend on licence entitlements.
claims.quote: Attended runs follow the entitlements of the user running the flow. A user whose license includes attended RPA isn't charged; a user whose license doesn't include it is charged $0.60 per run.

claims.claim: Unattended desktop runs in pay-as-you-go environments are charged per run.
claims.quote: Unattended runs are charged at $3.00 per run regardless of any capacity assigned to the environment.

claims.claim: No direct-trigger-specific rate or billing exception is published.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers licensing; Scheduled triggers desktop flows licensing. Opened pay-as-you-go-meters, power-automate-licensing/types and schedule-desktop-flows; these give general run-mode rules, not a distinct scheduled/direct-trigger price or exception.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects the documented desktop flow-run meter.
claims.quote: The Power Automate meters enable users to build and/or run premium Power Automate flows and to pay for their usage based on the number of times these flows run

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Change & support
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a direct-trigger-specific frequency limit.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers frequency limits; Scheduled triggers desktop flows limits. Opened schedule-desktop-flows and trigger-desktop-flows; schedules have configurable recurrence units but no published numerical trigger-frequency ceiling.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said which execution identity a directly triggered flow uses.
claims.quote: Connection reference | Yes | Select an existing connection reference, or select New connection reference to create one. User account | Conditional | When you enter credentials directly, enter the account in domain\username or username@domain.com format.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket identity gap with: 'Scheduled triggers (preview) select an execution connection reference for a machine or machine group; connection creation selects authentication and supplies credentials or a Windows credential. Identity details for broader event-trigger cases remain unpublished.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows; narrow the open question to those broader cases.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers identity machine session; Scheduled triggers desktop flows prerequisites. Opened schedule-desktop-flows and desktop-flow-connections; the scheduling page selects run mode and connection but does not describe a broader event-trigger session implementation.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a per-execution approval step for the planned direct event triggers.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers approvals; Scheduled triggers desktop flows approval. Opened schedule-desktop-flows, run-desktop-flows-url-shortcuts and governance; URL confirmations concern the separate URL route, and the scheduling page gives no per-run approval step.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not describe the data an event supplies to a desktop flow.

claims.quote: This simplifies automation design and reduces the effort required to connect desktop flows to business processes.

claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: The users eligible to use direct triggers are not yet published.
claims.quote: A work or school account that can access the target Power Platform environment. A published desktop flow that you own or co-own.
claims.fix: Replace the user-scope absence with: 'Scheduled triggers (preview) require a work or school account with access to the target environment and a published desktop flow the user owns or co-owns. User scope for broader event-trigger cases is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows.

claims.claim: No roles for configuring or managing direct triggers are published.
claims.quote: The Operator role includes organization-level permissions for the Flow trigger and Flow trigger instance tables. These permissions apply to the entire environment where the role is assigned, not just to records owned by the operator.
claims.fix: Replace the role gap with: 'The schedule owner and Power Automate Operator can manage Scheduled triggers (preview). Operator permissions for Flow trigger and Flow trigger instance apply throughout the environment, without granting permission to edit the underlying desktop flow.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows and remove advice implying that no schedule-management role is known.

claims.claim: Direct-trigger prerequisites are not yet published.
claims.quote: A machine or machine group registered in the same environment. A connection reference for the target machine or machine group. You can create the connection reference while creating the scheduled trigger.
claims.fix: Replace the prerequisite gap with: 'Scheduled triggers (preview) require a work or school account with environment access, a published desktop flow owned or co-owned by the user, a machine or machine group registered in the same environment, a connection reference, and the licensing and capacity for the selected run mode. Prerequisites for broader event-trigger cases remain unpublished.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows.

claims.claim: No rollout mechanics for direct triggering are published.
claims.quote: This feature is being gradually rolled out across regions and might not be available yet in your region.
claims.fix: Replace the rollout-mechanics absence with: 'Learn describes Scheduled triggers as a preview gradually rolling out across regions, which might not yet be available in your region. The roadmap still records In development and retains its January CY2027 preview and March CY2027 general availability targets; the documentation does not establish rollout of every planned event-trigger case.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows.

claims.claim: No source says that existing desktop flows or unrelated users automatically change when this capability arrives.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers default configuration; Scheduled triggers desktop flows prerequisites. Read the roadmap and schedule-desktop-flows; the latter describes creating and enabling schedules, not automatically adding triggers to existing flows or changing unrelated users.
